content:
We need to get the template from previous task make_8_lvl2-template_search-6, but that failed. We need to search for a template that matches the described transformation: cyclization of chalcones to flavanones via intramolecular Michael addition. The target molecule SMILES: O=C1C(C2=CC=CC=C2)OC3=CC=CC=C13. That's a flavanone (2-phenylchroman-4-one). The retrosynthetic step would break the C-C bond formed between the carbonyl carbon (C4) and the aromatic carbon (C2'?) Actually the Michael addition forms a C-C bond between the carbonyl alpha carbon (C2) and the beta carbon of the enone (C3). Also a C-O bond formed (the oxygen of the carbonyl becomes part of the heterocycle). The broken bond is a C-O (the phenolic OH? Wait description: "C-O bond is broken". In forward reaction, a C-O bond is broken (maybe the phenolic OH becomes part of the ether). So the precursor likely is a chalcone: a phenyl attached to an α,β-unsaturated ketone (aryl-CO-CH=CH-Ph). The chalcone SMILES: O=C(C=Cc1ccccc1)c2ccccc2? Actually chalcone: phenyl-CO-CH=CH-Ph. SMILES: O=C(C=CC1=CC=CC=C1)C2=CC=CC=C2. That's 1-phenyl-3-phenyl-2-propen-1-one. The flavanone is formed by intramolecular Michael addition of the phenolic OH? Wait flavanone formation from chalcone involves cyclization where the carbonyl oxygen attacks? Actually flavanone synthesis: chalcone undergoes intramolecular Michael addition of the phenolic oxygen? No, flavanone is a 2-phenylchroman-4-one, formed by cyclization of chalcone via nucleophilic attack of the carbonyl oxygen onto the β-carbon, forming a new C-O bond and a C-C bond? Let's recall: chalcone (aryl-CO-CH=CH-aryl) under base forms flavanone via intramolecular Michael addition of the carbonyl oxygen? Actually flavanone formation is via intramolecular aldol condensation? Wait typical flavanone synthesis: chalcone undergoes cyclization via nucleophilic attack of the phenolic OH (if present) to form flavanone? But the given target has an ether oxygen bridging the carbonyl carbon to the aromatic ring (forming a heterocycle). The precursor likely is a hydroxychalcone (2'-hydroxychalcone) where the phenolic OH attacks the β-carbon to form the heterocycle, breaking the O-H bond (C-O bond broken? Actually O-H bond broken). The description says a C-O bond is broken (maybe the phenolic O-H bond). So the precursor is a 2'-hydroxychalcone: O=C(C=CC1=CC=CC=C1)C2=CC=CC=C2O? Wait phenolic OH at ortho position relative to carbonyl? The flavanone ring includes oxygen bridging to carbonyl carbon, forming a heterocycle. The precursor would be a 2'-hydroxychalcone (ortho-hydroxy). SMILES: O=C(C=CC1=CC=CC=C1)C2=CC=CC=C2O? But the OH must be ortho to the carbonyl side chain. So the phenyl ring attached to carbonyl (A-ring) has an OH ortho to the carbonyl side chain. So SMILES: O=C(C=CC1=CC=CC=C1)C2=CC(O)=CC=C2. That's 2'-hydroxychalcone.

Thus applying retrosynthetic template should give that precursor. Possibly also other variations (different protecting groups). The task: "return all possible precursors of applying the template as the result of the task make_8_lvl2-template_search-6 to the molecule below". So we need to apply the template (which we need to retrieve). Since we don't have template ID, we can search for templates that match the target and produce plausible precursors. Use search_template_catalog_by_criteria with appropriate criteria: bonds broken/formed etc. The tool expects bonds in format "atomIdx-atomIdx". We don't know indices. Maybe we can search by functional groups formed/broken only. Let's try search with functional groups broken: ["ketones","aromatic hydroxyls"] and formed: ["ether oxygens"]. No bond criteria.
